pointers.sentence: Django's own, for a page not found, a server error, a bad request and a permission denied, are in `django/views/defaults.py`, and send a page built from `ERROR_PAGE_TEMPLATE` when the project has no template of its own; the root URLconf replaces any of them through `handler404` and its kin.

`URLResolver.resolve_error_handler` looks in the URLconf's module for a variable named `handler404`, or `handler400`, `handler403`, `handler500`, and takes the default of the same name from `django/conf/urls/__init__.py` when the module has none.
The defaults are Django's four (`django/urls/resolvers.py:URLResolver.resolve_error_handler`).

Each of the four is decorated with `requires_csrf_token`: the callable is that decorator's wrapper, and the `CsrfViewMiddleware` it runs never refuses the request ([A middleware as a decorator](middleware-decorators.md#the-decorators-made-this-way)) (`django/views/decorators/csrf.py:requires_csrf_token`, `django/views/decorators/csrf.py:_EnsureCsrfToken`).

Each of the four is decorated with `requires_csrf_token`: the callable is that decorator's wrapper, and the `CsrfViewMiddleware` it runs never refuses the request ([A middleware as a decorator](middleware-decorators.md#the-decorators-made-this-way)) (`django/views/decorators/csrf.py:requires_csrf_token`, `django/views/decorators/csrf.py:_EnsureCsrfToken`).

An error view can be called for a request that `CsrfViewMiddleware.process_view` never saw: a path that matches no pattern raises before any `process_view` hook runs (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler._get_response`).
The comment above the four views gives that as the reason for the decorator, in case a template needs `{% csrf_token %}` (`django/views/defaults.py`).
The 500 view is called through the same wrapper, but renders its template without the request, so its template cannot use it (`django/views/defaults.py:server_error`).
The one for 500 is called with the request alone (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:get_exception_response`, `django/core/handlers/exception.py:handle_uncaught_exception`).
The one for 500 is called with the request alone (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:get_exception_response`, `django/core/handlers/exception.py:handle_uncaught_exception`).

With the setting on, the 400 view is reached only for a multipart body that could not be parsed, since `response_for_exception` sends a `MultiPartParserError` to it without asking `settings.DEBUG`, which it asks for a `BadRequest` or a `SuspiciousOperation` (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:response_for_exception`).

The test for a string is there for the resolver's own exception, whose argument is a dictionary and not a sentence for a reader: it holds the path and, where the resolver got as far as trying patterns, the patterns that were tried (`django/views/defaults.py:page_not_found`).

An `Http404` with a message is named by it instead, here the one `SingleObjectMixin.get_object` raises for an article that does not exist (`django/views/generic/detail.py:SingleObjectMixin.get_object`):

`bad_request` hands its template the request and nothing about what was wrong; `permission_denied` passes the exception's text (`django/views/defaults.py:bad_request`, `django/views/defaults.py:permission_denied`).

`bad_request` hands its template the request and nothing about what was wrong; `permission_denied` passes the exception's text (`django/views/defaults.py:bad_request`, `django/views/defaults.py:permission_denied`).

`bad_request` passes nothing of the exception, as the comment above its last line says, "to not disclose any sensitive information" (`django/views/defaults.py:page_not_found`, `django/views/defaults.py:bad_request`).

`bad_request` passes nothing of the exception, as the comment above its last line says, "to not disclose any sensitive information" (`django/views/defaults.py:page_not_found`, `django/views/defaults.py:bad_request`).

It is the view of last resort: if it fails there is nothing behind it ([How an exception becomes a response](../handlers/exceptions.md#what-does-reach-the-server)) (`django/views/defaults.py:server_error`).
If the caller had asked for some other name, the exception is raised again: a project that names a template of its own is told when it is absent (`django/views/defaults.py`).
The other three put the string straight into a response (`django/views/defaults.py:page_not_found`).

The request then fails where the coroutine is first used as a response, and ends in a 500 or in an exception that leaves the handler ([What the handler asks of a view](callable.md#what-a-view-may-return)) (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:get_exception_response`, `django/core/handlers/exception.py:response_for_exception`, `django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.get_response`).

The request then fails where the coroutine is first used as a response, and ends in a 500 or in an exception that leaves the handler ([What the handler asks of a view](callable.md#what-a-view-may-return)) (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:get_exception_response`, `django/core/handlers/exception.py:response_for_exception`, `django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.get_response`).

The request then fails where the coroutine is first used as a response, and ends in a 500 or in an exception that leaves the handler ([What the handler asks of a view](callable.md#what-a-view-may-return)) (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:get_exception_response`, `django/core/handlers/exception.py:response_for_exception`, `django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.get_response`).

The system check of the error views binds each one's signature to positional arguments, two for 400, 403 and 404 and one for 500, and does not ask for a parameter named exception ([The URL checks, and listing the patterns](../urls/checks.md#the-four-checks-tagged-urls)) (`django/core/checks/urls.py:check_custom_error_handlers`).
The handler passes the exception by keyword (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:get_exception_response`).

What the replacement returns is kept as it is, status included: the handler chooses which error view to ask and never corrects the status of the answer, and `response_for_exception` renders a template response that has not been rendered ([How an exception becomes a response](../handlers/exceptions.md#which-exception-becomes-which-response)) (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:response_for_exception`).

A `handler404` that answers 200 is sent as a 200, and the handler logs nothing: `response_for_exception` logs no `Http404`, and `BaseHandler.get_response` logs only a status of 400 or more (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.get_response`).
